editorial: This report contains trends that have emerged for the first time today, without repeating records included in normal reports from the last 30 days.

items.title: open-webui/open-webui
items.summary: open-webui is a user-friendly interface that allows interaction with artificial intelligence models such as Ollama and OpenAI API. It offers a web-based interface developed to manage local or cloud-based language models.

items.title: lyogavin/airllm
items.summary: AirLLM makes it possible to run large language models with 70 billion parameters on graphics processors (GPUs) with only 4 GB of memory. This method allows AI models that require high hardware specifications to be run on limited resources.

items.title: microsoft/BitNet
items.summary: BitNet, developed by Microsoft, offers an official inference framework for 1-bit large language models (LLMs). Written in C++, this tool aims to optimize the execution of low-bit precision models.

items.title: Alishahryar1/free-claude-code
items.summary: Alishahryar1/free-claude-code is a Python project that provides free access to various tools such as Claude Code, Codex, and VSCode via terminal, application, IDE, or browser. It offers users over 1.3 billion free tokens, allowing them to use different models and interfaces through a single platform.

items.title: Passkeys are a trap
items.summary: Passkeys (passwordless login keys) are considered a trap that makes users dependent on specific platforms and complicates account access. The article argues that despite the security advantages of this technology, it restricts user control.

items.title: Total Annihilation, rebuilt for modern computers
items.summary: Total Annihilation is being redeveloped to run on modern computers. The Nanolathe project allows the classic strategy game Total Annihilation to be played in a way that is compatible with current hardware.

items.title: The gap in shared understanding of LLM capability is widening
items.summary: There is a serious disconnect in the common understanding of the capabilities of large language models. This situation shows that the gap between expectations regarding what artificial intelligence systems can do and their actual performance in the technology world is widening.

items.title: NYC's "Click to Cancel" rule is now in effect
items.summary: New York City's newly enacted "Click to Cancel" rule aims to simplify subscription cancellation processes. It mandates that businesses offer users the option to terminate subscriptions with the same ease as the method they used to sign up.

items.title: Fingerprints are the new cookies
items.summary: Digital fingerprint technology is replacing the cookies that websites use to track users. This method continues the tracking of personal data by identifying devices through browser configuration.

items.title: abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Quantized
items.summary: abenzerps/Qwen-Image-2.1-Uncensored-Quantized is an artificial intelligence model that performs text-to-image conversion. The model draws attention with its uncensored structure and quantized format.

items.title: Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo
items.summary: Shared on HuggingFace, Qwen/Qwen-Image-2.1-Turbo is an artificial intelligence model with text-to-image generation capabilities. It allows users to convert written prompts into visual content.

items.title: MetaKernelBench: Measuring GPU Kernel Knowledge Transfer Beyond Code
items.summary: MetaKernelBench measures how well artificial intelligence agents performing GPU kernel optimization can transfer the experiences they have gained across different domain-specific languages (DSL). The tool evaluates whether knowledge learned in one area improves solution processes in another language across 74 different problems.

items.title: Universal Textual Teaching for LLMs
items.summary: Universal Textual Teaching performs knowledge transfer in large language models (LLM) using a text-based method instead of training model parameters. This approach aims to overcome the limitations of traditional knowledge distillation methods by facilitating the reuse and interpretation of knowledge across different architectures.

items.title: Less from More: Reinforcing Sparse Video Reasoning from Dense References
items.summary: The article 'Less from More: Reinforcing Sparse Video Reasoning from Dense References' focuses on video-language models making reliable inferences with limited visual data instead of processing a large number of frames. The dense-to-sparse training framework called SAVER allows the model to make inferences with sparse frames by referencing dense video data during the training phase.

items.title: Encore: Few-Shot Agentic Discovery of Manipulation Strategies
items.summary: Encore uses few-shot learning to discover complex manipulation strategies in robotic tasks. The system processes given demonstrations as readable evidence rather than training data, accelerating the trial-and-error process of robotic agents.

items.title: S-Space: Exploring Spatial Workspace in Multimodal Language Models
items.summary: S-Space, which examines the spatial reasoning capabilities of multimodal language models, presents a linear representation subspace where object token representations encode coordinates on the horizontal, vertical, and depth axes. This study reveals that these spatial axes exist naturally within the internal structure of the models, independent of specific data.
